- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via meta.rollbackItem (sdk, the route ledger binds it to POST /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/rollback, selected by route anchor /:type/:name/rollback), rollbackItem (sdk, the bare tail of client method meta.rollbackItem, bound to POST /api/v1/meta/:type/:name/rollback))_

- `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx`  _(via /:type/:name/rollback (route, bridged from symbol rollbackMetaItem — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `123029be96651c38b8c7aacfc6ae2d623c667a66` — the merge of head `e5daf940f552900c0c35eeedd2b16b35af9a19a6` into base `258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 123029be96651c38b8c7aacfc6ae2d623c667a66 && git checkout 123029be96651c38b8c7aacfc6ae2d623c667a66
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275 e5daf940f552900c0c35eeedd2b16b35af9a19a6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275 && git merge --no-ff e5daf940f552900c0c35eeedd2b16b35af9a19a6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 258f4e6aaa5c1f75675b4195a35cb5da2ce5e275` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e5daf940f552900c0c35eeedd2b16b35af9a19a6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/sys-metadata-repository.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.restore-doors-save-refusal-family.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.credential-channel.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json, .changeset/25278-restore-doors-save-refusal-family.md + packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts, packages/rest/src/error-response.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.object-external-binding-managed-datasource-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.page-default-record-page-one-per-object-refused.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.api-endpoint-anonymous-elevated-flow-refused.ts

Inputs: card #25278 (body, claim 6352974944, os-dev-report 6354044792), PR #25312 (body, 6 files, net diff against `main`), and the 46 check-runs on the head: every one `success` or `skipped` (Check Changeset, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Type Check · workspace, Test Core 1–6, Dogfood Regression Gate, both single-writer guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard among them). Nothing built, run or re-run here.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept set — what a restore writes narrows (the card's ask).** `restoredBodyWriter` (`protocol.ts:7296–7306`) now awaits `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses` (`:7366–7396`) after the two judges it already asked (`savedItemNameRefusal`, `permissionSetOwnerBindingRefusal`) and before the R2 strip. `SysMetadataRepository.restoreVersion` awaits `deriveRestoredBody` at `sys-metadata-repository.ts:1669`, before the active row is read (`:1688`) and before `put` (`:1695`); the only writes in that method are the `put`, so a refused version stores nothing. **Right.** Both restore doors pass the writer (`protocol.ts:30233` revert, `:30586` rollback); `rollbackMetaItem`'s catch rethrows anything that is not a `ConflictError` (`:30664–30683`); `revertCommit`'s per-item catch lands it in `failed[]` with `clientFacingFailureCode` (`:30301–30303`). The card's pins (refusal answers the save door's refusal, stores nothing; an acceptable version still restores) are measured in the new file: 7 cases x {rollback, revert} x {refusal, control}, with a byte-identical snapshot of rows, history length and registry after each refusal. **Right.**

**Census, checked judge by judge against the save door at this head (`protocol.ts:24196–24325`).** Each restore call is the save door's own function, no rule copied:
- 1 `runtimeHookWithoutBodyRefusal(type, body, name)` — same three arguments (`:24196` vs `:7373`). Right.
- 2 `defaultRecordPageSaveRefusal(type, body, name, 'restored')` — same judge; the verb union widens by `'restored'` (`:22531`) and the verb is used only in the sentence (`:22588`). The saved name is excluded from the holders, so a page whose current active row already holds the default restores. Right.
- 3 `externalBindingSaveRefusal(type, body, name)` — same judge, both halves (object at `external`, datasource at `schemaMode`, `:22651–22666`), read against the live store. The save door passes a fourth argument `request.writeFace` (`:24220`); the restore passes none, so the refusal's sentence is rendered on the default face (`specValidationFindings`, `:4246–4275`) while `code`, `status` and `issues[]` are identical. The rollback request declares no face (`:30439–30446`), so there is nothing to pass; the REST route forwards `issues[]` as-is (`error-response.ts:593`). Right; prose-only difference, named here so it is not read as a copied rule.
- 4 `anonymousElevatedFlowRefusal(type, body, name)` — same judge; the save door skips it for drafts and `migrate-stored` (`:24230`), a restore is an active write from a protocol door, so asking it unconditionally is the save door's own condition. Right.
- 5 `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules({ state: 'active', packageId: binding, source, restoredCredentialPaths })` — same judge, same early-returns (`package-author` channel, `migrate-stored`, `:7548–7564`). The credential-paths provider differs from the save door's `restoredCredentialPathsFor` (`:9961–9993`), which unions the carry-forward's redacted paths with the channel's held paths; the restore passes only the channel's held paths (`:7390`). Right: `restoreVersion` performs no carry-forward (the history body is written as it is), so the carried half does not exist on a restore, and this is the exact shape `promoteDraftForPublish` passes (`:26032–26034`). The one input that differs from the save door: a flow stored on the canonicalizer's fallback is judged by the save door in its D2-converted spelling (`flowGateVerdictBody`, `:24257`) and by the restore in its stored spelling. That is the stored-shape question (③, open question), not a copied rule.
- 6 `runAuthoringGate({ type, name, state: 'active', body })` on `authoringChannel !== 'package-author'` — same function, same condition (`:24319` vs `:7393`). Right.
- 7 ADR-0070 D1 `readOnlyBaseCreateError` not asked — D1 judges a package the caller names for a new item (`:24394` on base); `restoreVersion` writes into the active row's own `package_id` (`sys-metadata-repository.ts:1688–1704`). Reason written in the code (`:7347–7353`). Right.
- 8 credential channel `store` not asked — `restoredBodyDerivation` only strips (`:7255–7258`); the restore never stores a credential; the moved R2 pin (`protocol.credential-channel.test.ts:272–279`, `['heldPaths:active', 'strip']`) records exactly the new read and still proves no `store`. Right.
- Zod gate not asked — reason in the code (`:7340–7346`); see ③.

**Public surface.** `SysMetadataRepository` is exported (`index.ts:142`); its `restoreVersion` option `deriveRestoredBody` widens from a synchronous callback to one that may also return a promise (`sys-metadata-repository.ts:1616`), additive for every caller, and the single implementer awaits it (`:1669`). No other `restoreVersion` implementation or `deriveRestoredBody` consumer exists at the head (`git grep` over `packages/`). `restoredBodyWriter`, `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses` and `defaultRecordPageSaveRefusal` are private. The published metadata accept set does not move; what a restore WRITES narrows. Right.

**Engine-double ledger.** `scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json` gains three rows for the new test file's double (`delete`, `findOne`, `update`), the gate's mechanical record of the double it already checks; the double asserts the producer's own dispatch predicates (`assertEngineDeleteDispatch`, `assertEngineUpdateDispatch`, `assertEngineFindOnePredicate`). Right.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25278-restore-doors-save-refusal-family.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`, a BREAKING banner with FROM → TO and the one-line fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (already-registered ...)` naming three ledger ids that exist on `main` at `97967a9` (`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.*`), none added by this diff. The diff adds no rule and changes no schema (`packages/spec/**` untouched), so `already-registered` is the fitting category; a narrowed kind on a moved package takes at least `minor` (AGENTS.md §3) — **matches what the diff publishes**. The PR body carries the same two declaration lines. `Check Changeset` and `Lint · CI, release & engine gates` are green on the head.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — read on the PR body and the changeset, consistent with the diff: no widening anywhere; a restore refuses what it accepted.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev deviations (os-dev-report 6354044792), each answered:
1. Ledger file outside the claimed surface — accepted: the gate writes it for the new double; no hand content.
2. R2 pin moved from `['strip']` to `['heldPaths:active', 'strip']` — accepted: the restore now asks the runtime rules with the channel's held paths before the strip (`protocol.ts:7303` then `:7304`); the guarded property (no `store`, current secret kept, `held.get(...) === V2`) is still pinned.
3. Reviewer request left to the seat — not a contract matter.
4. Docs drift: the four flagged pages were read at the head; none states what a rollback or revert refuses (the only rollback line is the route table row at `content/docs/kernel/contracts/metadata-service.mdx:502`). No doc edit owed.

Open question (Zod parse on a restored body): **A, escalated for a ruling, not decided here.** The card names the family as the refusals "after the Zod gate", so leaving the parse unasked is inside the card; whether today's parse may refuse a stored version (and, the same question, whether a fallback-stored flow is judged in its stored or its converted spelling, ① item 5) is the ADR-0087 stored-shape question. The adopting seat should file it as its own card; nothing in this PR forecloses either answer.

Dev out-of-scope findings, judged:
- Stale comment `packages/rest/src/meta-item-history-routes.ts:746` ("rollback runs no content gate at all") — false after this PR; class c, in a file outside the claim's surface. Left to the seat, as the dev said; the route's behaviour is already right (`handleRouteError` forwards the thrown 4xx with `issues[]`).
- Pre-Zod save-door refusals not asked by a restore (`protocol.ts:23635` package mismatch, `:23683` NAMESPACE_PREFIX, `:23711` protection block, `:23848` DESTRUCTIVE_CHANGE, `:23877` layered-envelope body, `:23915` name, `:23926` owner, `:23942` view-container collision). The dev's stated reason, "each judges a request or a diff against the live row", holds for the package, prefix, destructive and collision judges; it is imprecise for `protectionBlockRefusal` (`:1136`, a body judge) and the layered-envelope check (`:23877`, a body judge). Both shapes are refused by the save door itself, so only a door other than the save door could have stored them; they are outside the family the card names, and no restore was measured against them. Class c observation for the seat; not a defect of this PR. Named here so the next reader does not take the blanket reason as measured.

Nothing in the diff touches the datasource-admin service (#25277), the stored-shape detector (#25279) or `packages/spec/**`, as the claim forbade.
